fieldMarks: Brown back with gray on shoulders, neck and head; sides and belly somewhat yellowish
Eyes outlined by a white ring; ears larger than typical ground squirrels
Lacks dorsal stripes and spots; short tail (59-79 mm) coloured like the back; large claws
behavior: Very vocal: chirp and churr alarm calls; flicks the tail in aggression
One of the least social ground squirrels
Emerges from hibernation in early spring; dormant again from late July to early September
Eats seeds, flowers, stems, leaves and roots; insects in late summer; sometimes carrion
habitat: Well-drained upland slopes of dry grassland or shrub steppe (especially sagebrush) with loose sandy soil; mountain meadows and talus slopes from 1,500 m to above timberline.
range: Interior western US in three isolated areas: southeastern Oregon (formerly), southwestern Idaho and north-central Nevada; northeastern Idaho and southwestern Montana; northeastern Utah, southern Wyoming, northern Colorado and extreme western Nebraska.
